fact.title: One of the busiest websites on Earth is an adult video site.
fact.desc: It reported about 115 million visits a day in 2019, and in 2018 it sent 4,403 petabytes of video: about 140 GB every second, busiest late at night. Here is how a site like that stays up.
points: Each video is split into pieces a few seconds long, in several qualities. Any server can send any piece, and a player can switch quality between pieces when the network slows.
The CDN does the heavy lifting
Servers in hundreds of cities keep the popular pieces close to viewers. Almost every request ends there; the company's own servers see a small share.
Plan for the peak, not the average
Traffic is far higher at night than in the afternoon. Capacity is sized for the busiest hour, and the CDN absorbs the surges.
fact.source: Figures from the site's own published yearly reports for 2018 and 2019.

learn.title: Pick your level
learn.desc: Each level is a short path: read a little, try it in the Lab, then solve challenges for stars. Your progress stays in this browser.

levels.label: Beginner
levels.desc: New to system design. Start with how programs talk to each other and what happens when too many people show up at once.

steps.title: Read: APIs, the main types and where to use each
steps.why: Every design starts with how its parts talk.

steps.title: Try: run the example design in the Lab
steps.why: See load, latency and cost move as traffic flows.

steps.title: Challenge: too much for one server
steps.why: Scale out, and check what the database can take.

steps.title: Challenge: lunch and dinner rush
steps.why: Size for the peak without paying for it all day.

levels.label: Intermediate
levels.desc: You know the parts. Now make them hold up under spikes and heavy reads, and keep the bill sensible.

steps.title: Read: the numbers behind a design
steps.why: Latencies and quick arithmetic for sizing.

steps.title: Challenge: survive IND vs PAK
steps.why: A CDN, a live stream and 3.5 crore people at once.

steps.title: Challenge: the menu everyone reads
steps.why: Where a cache earns its place.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.desc: Failure is normal. Design for the crash you know is coming, and for data you can't afford to lose.

steps.title: Challenge: the cache restarts at dinner
steps.why: A cold cache can take the database down with it.

steps.title: Challenge: don't lose an order
steps.why: Write-back is fast until it isn't.

steps.title: Build: import your own architecture and run it
steps.why: Type in a system you know and watch where it breaks.

dashboard.title: Start with your level
dashboard.text: Pick Beginner, Intermediate or Advanced. Each is a short path of reading, trying and solving, and it ticks itself off as you go.

dashboard.title: Everything is in these tabs
dashboard.text: Concepts, Components and Interview Questions are the library; Quick Notes and Did you know are short reads. Learn is where you are now.

dashboard.title: The Lab
dashboard.text: Build a system from cloud components, send traffic through it and watch what breaks. Challenges give you up to three stars each.

dashboard.title: Come back to this tour
dashboard.text: Press Tour any time. Your progress and designs stay in this browser.

lab.title: Components
lab.text: Drag a component onto the canvas, or tap it. Each has a realistic price and limit; select it to see what it is like in real life.

lab.title: Your design
lab.text: Connect two components by dragging from the dot on the right of one to the dot on the left of the other. Click an arrow to remove it.

lab.title: Run traffic
lab.text: Send the Clients' requests through your design on a simulated clock. Load, latency and crashes show on every component.

lab.title: $200,000 of credit
lab.text: Every design starts with virtual AWS credit, spent at its hourly cost while traffic runs.

lab.title: Challenges
lab.text: Scenarios with goals and up to three stars each, from one overloaded server to a cache that crashes at dinner.

lab.title: Your designs
lab.text: Start new designs, duplicate one with fresh credit, import your own architecture as text, or export a design as JSON.

landingLab.title: Can your design survive IND vs PAK?
landingLab.desc: On 14 October 2023, 3.5 crore people watched India play Pakistan live on one streaming app, all at the same time. Here is the real Lab with that match loaded. Add what's missing, press Score, and see if the stream holds from the toss to the last over.
landingLab.note: Peak of 3.5 crore people watching at once: ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023, India vs Pakistan, as reported by the broadcaster. The app here is made up. Each player fetches a 4-second chunk every 4 seconds; capacities and prices are rules of thumb.
